Definition: of uncertain derivation; a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn:--break of day.
BiblicalUsage: After Paul raised Eutychus, he went up and broke bread and talked a long while, even till break of day, and so departed. The word means the dawn, the first ray of morning.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the dawn after a long night of preaching is a small picture of the resurrection morning, when the talking will give way to the seeing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
